messages:
omar: Heads up — had an overnight layover in Madrid after a delayed flight home. Carrier rerouted me and I had to book a last-minute room and a transfer to the airport. Original itinerary was same-day; company paid outbound but not the surprise night. Can I claim the hotel + taxi + dinner under disruption policy? cc @people-ops

people-ops: Sorry about the disruption. Short answer: yes if you can show the flight delay/cancellation notice. We cover reasonable incremental costs (lodging + meals + transport) when it's beyond your control. Attach proof and receipts.

omar: Proof attached (email from airline + new boarding pass). Hotel was €95, taxi €34, dinner €22. I used a ride app and have the receipt screenshot. The hotel folio is digital and lists total only; no nightly breakdown.

finance: For hotel folios without nightly itemization we accept either: (a) a hotel itemized folio requested from the property, OR (b) a short attestation explaining why itemization isn't available + manager approval. Please create a single incident expense in Expensify named `flight-disruption-2026-10-10` and attach everything.

omar: What about per diem? The layover meant I missed one company-paid overnight but was that eligible for per diem since it was travel-related?

travel-bot: Policy excerpt: "Subsistence (meals) for unplanned, business-related overnight delays are eligible up to local per diem caps. Per diem applies only for days including business travel; pro-rate where applicable. Receipts required for meals above the per diem threshold."

people-ops: Practically: claim the actual meal receipts for the disrupted night. If total meals exceed the per diem cap for Madrid, finance will reimburse up to the cap. The incidental portion of per diem is covered too.

omar: Ok. Also the taxi tip was cash — can we accept a lost-receipt attestation for cash tip?

finance: Yes, up to €50 we accept a lost-receipt attestation for small cash items with manager approval. Add a note in the expense: `cash-tip-attestation: €5 taxi`.

omar: Last Q — I had a corporate card hold on the original refundable leg. I booked the emergency hotel on my personal card. If the airline issues a voucher/refund later, will you net it?

people-ops: We'll reconcile. If you get a refund/voucher for the original paid item, upload proof and we'll adjust the reimbursement. If reimbursement already paid, you may need to return the excess or we will deduct at reconciliation.

omar: Thanks, submitting now. Appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
